title: Camera Blind-Spot Duration from Occlusion
dataSources: Object detections (`frigate:event`), camera health (`camera:health`), alarm state changes (`alarm:event`), smart-lock access (`lock:access`), plate and gate events (`gate:event`), and doorbell delivery telemetry (`doorbell:event`).
app: Home-security telemetry from Frigate and Blue Iris detections, camera health feeds, smart locks, alarm panels, doorbells, and gate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and Home Assistant integrations.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=camera:health event="occlusion"
| stats sum(duration_sec) as blind_spot_sec by camera
| eval blind_spot_min=round(blind_spot_sec/60,1)
| sort - blind_spot_min
description: Measures how long each camera view was blocked by fog, spider webs, dirt, or a moved object.
value: A camera can stay online while still being useless, so occlusion duration is a practical way to monitor true coverage quality.
implementation: Send occlusion or obstruction events from Frigate, Blue Iris, or custom image-health checks into Splunk.
visualization: Bar chart of blind-spot minutes by camera.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how long each camera was partly blocked, so you do not mistake a working camera for a useful one.
